tier1Summary:
After the US midterms, diplomacy on the [[e:2026 Iran war]] is moving: [[p:Donald Trump]] met Qatar's prime minister and cited "positive momentum", Iran offers to reopen Hormuz in two days on its terms, and Brent fell to about $92, though Washington still enforces its blockade and calls Tehran's demands outrageous.

The Saudi–[[p:Houthis|Houthi]] war is pulling in the region: Turkey ratified the [[e:Mecca defence pact|Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]], and AFP sources report Syrian troops heading to the Saudi–Yemeni border, which Damascus disputes. Israel's new Knesset is sworn in today as [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] courts Likud and Netanyahu pitches his own unity government. Gaza's tent camps flooded and West Bank settler attacks hit a record.

Elsewhere: US-mediated Russia–Ukraine talks opened in Abu Dhabi.

segmentItems.text: [[p:Donald Trump]] met Qatar's prime minister on Iran and cited "positive momentum", calling new strikes "quite unlikely"; [[p:Marco Rubio]] says Iran's demands are outrageous. Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz within two days if the US ends the war, lifts sanctions and the blockade. Brent fell to about $91.6.
segmentItems.outlet: Al Jazeera; AFP (via Arab News); Gulf News

segmentItems.text: The US disabled the cargo ship M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman on 7 Nov for running the blockade; Iranian officials claim new US strikes on Qeshm Island on 8 Nov, unconfirmed by Washington.
segmentItems.outlet: Al Jazeera; Gulf News; Times of Israel

segmentItems.text: Turkey's parliament ratified the [[e:Mecca defence pact|Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]] 279–119 on 4 Nov. [[p:Yaşar Güler]] {{note: Turkish general who was chief of the General Staff before becoming defence minister in 2023.}} says support for Riyadh aims at deterrence, not fighting the Houthis.

AFP's Yemeni sources say up to 3,000 Syrian troops are deploying to the Saudi–Yemeni border against the [[p:Houthis]] {{note: Zaydi Shia movement that began in northern Yemen in the 1990s under Hussein al-Houthi.}}, days after [[p:Ahmed al-Sharaa]] signed a defence deal and $403m in loans in Riyadh. Syria's state agency denies sending troops to Yemen "at this time".

[[p:Houthis|Houthi]] missiles and drones kept targeting Riyadh and the East–West pipeline on 8–9 Nov. Yemen's government claims gains in Lahj and al-Jawf; the Houthis report over 100 Saudi strikes in a day. Neither claim is verified.

The new [[p:Knesset]] is sworn in today. [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] invites [[p:Likud]] to join a government under him; [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]] counters with a unity government under himself. [[p:Avigdor Lieberman]] backs Eisenkot on the Speaker but rejects relying on Arab-led parties; [[p:Shas]] stays with Netanyahu.

The army ended its ten-day Hebron operation on 2 Nov after displacing over 3,000 people, per the municipality. [[p:Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs|OCHA]] logged 457 damaging settler attacks in October, a monthly record since 2006.

A storm flooded about 70,000 Gaza tents and killed at least five, Gaza authorities say; the health ministry counts 1,613 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire. The [[p:Board of Peace]] urged Israel to admit winter supplies.
segmentItems.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan

segmentItems.text: Israeli strikes continued across south Lebanon on 9 Nov; PM [[p:Nawaf Salam]] says avoiding a new war is the priority as residents stockpile.
segmentItems.opinion: reporter's view (Al Jazeera piece includes analysts' views)
segmentItems.thread: Lebanon: Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli occupation

segmentItems.text: The US asked Iraq to close all Iran crossings but two; FM [[p:Fuad Hussein]] calls that hard and says Iraq agreed a Hormuz export lane with Washington.
segmentItems.outlet: Reuters (via Arab News); Khaleej Times (citing INA)

segmentItems.text: France blamed an [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] unit for October's supermarket refrigerator hack, summoned Iran's ambassador and will seek EU sanctions.
Iran executed three January protesters in Karaj; [[p:Iran Human Rights]] counts at least 81 political executions this year.

tier1Check.text: US-mediated Russia–Ukraine talks opened in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round since February, with [[p:Jared Kushner]] and [[p:Steve Witkoff]] mediating and security guarantees on the agenda. Russia's delegation under [[p:Vladimir Medinsky]] includes the GRU chief.

readInFull.title: Ahead of the Knesset swearing-in: agreements, disputes and what the Haredim will do
readInFull.reporter: Moran Azulai, Yuval Karni et al.
readInFull.why: The clearest map of Israel's coalition arithmetic: what Lieberman demands, what UTJ wants on the draft law, and why Shas is the swing problem for [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]].

readInFull.title: Yemen government forces claim new advances as Houthi border attacks resume
readInFull.why: A front-by-front picture of the Saudi–[[p:Houthis|Houthi]] war that separates each side's claims from what can be verified.

watchThisWeek.text: Mekelle: deadline for handing in unlicensed firearms, followed by house-to-house searches.
France: Lecornu's 'social conference' on wages on 9 Nov; Senate takes up the social-security budget 9–18 Nov.
Trilateral US–Russia–Ukraine working-level talks in Abu Dhabi, 10–11 Nov. Russia's team is led by [[p:Vladimir Medinsky]], Ukraine's by [[p:Rustem Umerov]].
Final calls in the uncalled Senate races in Alaska (Sullivan vs Peltola) and Mississippi (Hyde-Smith vs Colom).
Sweden: Kristersson reports back to the Speaker; the Centre Party wants answers from both blocs by 13 Nov.
UN Security Council emergency meeting on the Komyshuvakha strike, requested by Latvia (date not yet set).
Gagauzia People's Assembly and Bashkan elections in Moldova.
Post-election push on the Gaza plan: [[p:Board of Peace]] and [[p:International Stabilization Force]] deployment, plus France's promised conference for the Lebanese army 'after' Israel's election
Whether any Russian diesel cargo is actually delivered to the US under the October arrangement.
Whether Transnistrian leader [[p:Vadim Krasnoselsky]] returns from Moscow and how the five-year exit ban is applied.
Operation Carthage: anti-corruption court rulings on custody for the SBU and police suspects.
Poland: Constitutional Tribunal judges' assembly on lifting Święczkowski's immunity and detaining him.
Washington's reply to Iran's two-day plan and the Qatari-backed draft (day 1: blockade lifted and some funds released; day 2: Hormuz reopens, then nuclear talks).
Iraq: whether more Iran border crossings close under the US Treasury request (Mandali closes temporarily from 13 Nov).
